question_text: Mountain climbers sometimes feel breathless at high altitudes because their blood struggles to carry enough oxygen to their muscles. Which blood cells are responsible for carrying oxygen in the first place?
raw_text: Mountain climbers sometimes feel breathless at high altitudes because their blood struggles to carry enough oxygen to their muscles. Which blood cells are responsible for carrying oxygen in the first place?
explanation: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, a protein that binds oxygen in the lungs and carries it to tissues throughout the body.

question_text: A government report warns that a certain fuel source took millions of years to form underground and cannot be replaced once used up. Which of these fits this description?
raw_text: A government report warns that a certain fuel source took millions of years to form underground and cannot be replaced once used up. Which of these fits this description?
explanation: Coal is a fossil fuel formed over millions of years from buried plant matter, making it a non-renewable resource once it is used up.

question_text: On a hot day, a gardener notices tiny droplets forming on the underside of a clear plastic bag tied over a plant's leaves. Which process is releasing this water vapour from the leaves?
raw_text: On a hot day, a gardener notices tiny droplets forming on the underside of a clear plastic bag tied over a plant's leaves. Which process is releasing this water vapour from the leaves?
explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from plant leaves through tiny pores called stomata.

question_text: A tailor uses a tool with two blades joined at a pivot point to cut fabric with less effort than tearing it by hand. Which simple machine is at work here?
raw_text: A tailor uses a tool with two blades joined at a pivot point to cut fabric with less effort than tearing it by hand. Which simple machine is at work here?
explanation: Scissors function as a double lever, with the pivot (fulcrum) located at the joint between the two blades.

question_text: Astronauts returning to Earth notice a thin blue haze surrounding the planet from space — a blanket of gases held in place by gravity. What is this layer called?
raw_text: Astronauts returning to Earth notice a thin blue haze surrounding the planet from space — a blanket of gases held in place by gravity. What is this layer called?
explanation: The atmosphere is the layer of gases, mainly nitrogen and oxygen, that surrounds Earth and is held close by gravity.

question_text: A wildlife photographer waits all winter to spot a particular animal, but it has slowed its heartbeat and is sleeping deep inside a cave to conserve energy until spring. Which animal behaviour is this?
raw_text: A wildlife photographer waits all winter to spot a particular animal, but it has slowed its heartbeat and is sleeping deep inside a cave to conserve energy until spring. Which animal behaviour is this?
explanation: Bears hibernate during winter, lowering their metabolism to conserve energy when food is scarce.

question_text: An X-ray technician explains to a patient that without a certain rigid internal framework, the body's organs would have no protection and no way to stand upright. What is this framework called?
raw_text: An X-ray technician explains to a patient that without a certain rigid internal framework, the body's organs would have no protection and no way to stand upright. What is this framework called?
explanation: The skeleton gives the body structure, protects internal organs, and works with muscles to allow movement.

question_text: If you could remove every other gas from the air except the one we actually breathe in to survive, you would be left with about one-fifth of the original air. Which gas is this?
raw_text: If you could remove every other gas from the air except the one we actually breathe in to survive, you would be left with about one-fifth of the original air. Which gas is this?
explanation: Oxygen makes up about 21% of Earth's atmosphere and is the gas our bodies use for respiration.

question_text: Weather forecasters predict that clouds will soon release moisture onto the ground, either as rain, snow, or hail depending on temperature. What general term covers all of these forms of falling water?
raw_text: Weather forecasters predict that clouds will soon release moisture onto the ground, either as rain, snow, or hail depending on temperature. What general term covers all of these forms of falling water?
explanation: Precipitation is any form of water, liquid or solid, that falls from clouds to Earth's surface.

question_text: After a bee visits a flower and pollen is transferred, a small swollen part at the base of the flower begins to grow larger and eventually ripens. Which part is this?
raw_text: After a bee visits a flower and pollen is transferred, a small swollen part at the base of the flower begins to grow larger and eventually ripens. Which part is this?
explanation: After fertilisation, the ovary develops into a fruit, while the ovules inside develop into seeds.

question_text: An electrician checks how much electricity is flowing through a wire using a meter that displays a reading in a specific unit named after a French physicist. Which unit is this?
raw_text: An electrician checks how much electricity is flowing through a wire using a meter that displays a reading in a specific unit named after a French physicist. Which unit is this?
explanation: Electric current is measured in Amperes (A), named after André-Marie Ampère.

question_text: An electrician wraps the metal wires of a plug with a stretchy black material before handling it, to avoid getting shocked. Which property of this material makes it safe to use this way?
raw_text: An electrician wraps the metal wires of a plug with a stretchy black material before handling it, to avoid getting shocked. Which property of this material makes it safe to use this way?
options: It is a good conductor of heat
raw_options: It is a good conductor of heat
explanation: Rubber is a good electrical insulator — it does not allow current to pass through easily, which is why it's used to coat wires and tool handles.

question_text: A crow is observed eating both fallen grain and small insects in the same afternoon. What term describes this kind of diet?
raw_text: A crow is observed eating both fallen grain and small insects in the same afternoon. What term describes this kind of diet?
explanation: Omnivores eat both plant and animal matter — crows, like humans and bears, are common examples.

question_text: Despite hurtling through space at thousands of kilometres per hour, Earth never flies off into deep space, but instead keeps circling the Sun year after year. Which force is responsible for this?
raw_text: Despite hurtling through space at thousands of kilometres per hour, Earth never flies off into deep space, but instead keeps circling the Sun year after year. Which force is responsible for this?
explanation: The Sun's gravitational pull keeps Earth and other planets in their orbits, constantly pulling them inward as they move forward.

question_text: A doctor reviewing a blood test explains that a rising count of a certain cell type usually means the body is actively fighting off an infection. Which blood cells are being discussed?
raw_text: A doctor reviewing a blood test explains that a rising count of a certain cell type usually means the body is actively fighting off an infection. Which blood cells are being discussed?
explanation: White blood cells are part of the immune system, and their numbers often rise when the body is fighting bacteria or viruses.

question_text: An ice cube left on a kitchen counter slowly turns into a puddle of water, but if you froze that water again, you would get ice once more. What type of change is melting?
raw_text: An ice cube left on a kitchen counter slowly turns into a puddle of water, but if you froze that water again, you would get ice once more. What type of change is melting?
explanation: Melting is a physical change because the water's chemical composition (H₂O) stays the same — only its state changes, and it can be reversed by freezing.

question_text: Scientists studying rising global temperatures point to a particular gas, released heavily by vehicles and factories, that traps heat in the atmosphere like a blanket. Which gas is this?
raw_text: Scientists studying rising global temperatures point to a particular gas, released heavily by vehicles and factories, that traps heat in the atmosphere like a blanket. Which gas is this?
explanation: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere, significantly contributing to the greenhouse effect and global warming.

question_text: A neurologist explains to a patient that all their thoughts, memories, and decisions are controlled by one organ that also coordinates the rest of the body. Which organ is this?
raw_text: A neurologist explains to a patient that all their thoughts, memories, and decisions are controlled by one organ that also coordinates the rest of the body. Which organ is this?
explanation: The brain is the control centre of the nervous system, responsible for thought, memory, and coordinating body functions.

question_text: A child pulls back a slingshot's rubber band before releasing it to launch a small pebble forward. What type of energy is stored in the stretched rubber band just before release?
raw_text: A child pulls back a slingshot's rubber band before releasing it to launch a small pebble forward. What type of energy is stored in the stretched rubber band just before release?
explanation: A stretched elastic object stores elastic potential energy, which is released as kinetic energy once the object returns to its original shape.

question_text: Engineers launch a metal structure into orbit around Earth so astronauts can live and conduct experiments aboard it for months at a time. Which of these is this kind of object?
raw_text: Engineers launch a metal structure into orbit around Earth so astronauts can live and conduct experiments aboard it for months at a time. Which of these is this kind of object?
explanation: The ISS is an artificial (man-made) satellite orbiting Earth, built for scientific research, unlike the Moon, which is a natural satellite.

question_text: A balloon is left out in the hot midday Sun, and by afternoon, it appears noticeably more inflated than it was in the morning, even though no extra air was added. Why might this happen?
raw_text: A balloon is left out in the hot midday Sun, and by afternoon, it appears noticeably more inflated than it was in the morning, even though no extra air was added. Why might this happen?
options: The gas inside cooled and contracted
The gas inside heated and expanded
raw_options: The gas inside cooled and contracted
The gas inside heated and expanded
correct_answer: The gas inside heated and expanded
explanation: Heating a gas increases the kinetic energy of its molecules, causing it to expand and occupy more volume — making the balloon appear more inflated.

question_text: An optician explains that light entering the eye eventually strikes a layer at the very back, which converts it into signals the brain can understand. Which part of the eye is this?
raw_text: An optician explains that light entering the eye eventually strikes a layer at the very back, which converts it into signals the brain can understand. Which part of the eye is this?
explanation: The retina contains light-sensitive cells that convert light into electrical signals, which travel to the brain via the optic nerve.

question_text: A farmer notices that his hens regularly lay eggs that hatch into chicks, continuing the cycle of life on the farm. What is this life process called?
raw_text: A farmer notices that his hens regularly lay eggs that hatch into chicks, continuing the cycle of life on the farm. What is this life process called?
explanation: Reproduction is the process by which organisms produce new individuals of their own kind, ensuring the continuation of a species.

question_text: A chef chooses a particular type of pan because it heats up quickly and evenly when placed on a stove, unlike a wooden spoon resting beside it. What property of metal explains this?
raw_text: A chef chooses a particular type of pan because it heats up quickly and evenly when placed on a stove, unlike a wooden spoon resting beside it. What property of metal explains this?
options: Metal is a poor conductor of heat
Metal is an excellent conductor of heat
raw_options: Metal is a poor conductor of heat
Metal is an excellent conductor of heat
correct_answer: Metal is an excellent conductor of heat
explanation: Metals have free-moving electrons that quickly transfer thermal energy, making them excellent heat conductors compared to materials like wood.

question_text: A botanist examines a leaf under a microscope and finds tiny pores on its surface that open and close to control gas exchange. What are these pores called?
raw_text: A botanist examines a leaf under a microscope and finds tiny pores on its surface that open and close to control gas exchange. What are these pores called?
explanation: Stomata are tiny pores on leaves that regulate the exchange of gases (CO₂ in, O₂ out) and the release of water vapour.

question_text: A camper lights a candle inside a tent at night so the inside glows, unlike a mirror placed nearby which only bounces light from elsewhere. What makes the candle different from the mirror?
raw_text: A camper lights a candle inside a tent at night so the inside glows, unlike a mirror placed nearby which only bounces light from elsewhere. What makes the candle different from the mirror?
options: The candle produces its own light
The mirror produces its own light
raw_options: The candle produces its own light
The mirror produces its own light
correct_answer: The candle produces its own light
explanation: A candle flame generates its own light through combustion, while a mirror can only reflect light produced by another source.

question_text: A farmer notices that her cow gives birth to a fully formed calf, unlike the hens on the same farm which lay eggs that hatch later. What term describes animals like the cow?
raw_text: A farmer notices that her cow gives birth to a fully formed calf, unlike the hens on the same farm which lay eggs that hatch later. What term describes animals like the cow?
explanation: Viviparous animals, like mammals, give birth to live young that developed inside the mother's body, unlike oviparous animals which lay eggs.

question_text: Astronomers studying a particular planet find that it spins so slowly on its axis that a single day there lasts longer than the time it takes to orbit the Sun. Which planet is this?
raw_text: Astronomers studying a particular planet find that it spins so slowly on its axis that a single day there lasts longer than the time it takes to orbit the Sun. Which planet is this?
explanation: Venus rotates so slowly that one day (about 243 Earth days) is longer than its year (about 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun).

question_text: A household stove burns a fuel piped in from underground reserves, mostly made of one simple hydrocarbon gas. What is this main component called?
raw_text: A household stove burns a fuel piped in from underground reserves, mostly made of one simple hydrocarbon gas. What is this main component called?
explanation: Natural gas is primarily composed of methane (CH₄), a simple hydrocarbon commonly used as a household and industrial fuel.

question_text: A forest floor covered in fallen leaves and dead insects is gradually cleared away by fungi and bacteria, which break down this matter and return nutrients to the soil. What term describes these organisms?
raw_text: A forest floor covered in fallen leaves and dead insects is gradually cleared away by fungi and bacteria, which break down this matter and return nutrients to the soil. What term describes these organisms?
explanation: Decomposers (fungi, bacteria) break down dead plants and animals, recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.

question_text: An engineer watches a rocket launch and explains to a curious student that the rocket moves upward precisely because hot gas is being forcefully expelled downward. Which law explains this action-reaction relationship?
raw_text: An engineer watches a rocket launch and explains to a curious student that the rocket moves upward precisely because hot gas is being forcefully expelled downward. Which law explains this action-reaction relationship?
explanation: Newton's Third Law: for every action there's an equal and opposite reaction. Gas pushed backward propels the rocket forward.

question_text: What is the pH range of acidic substances?
raw_text: What is the pH range of acidic substances?
explanation: On the pH scale (0-14), values below 7 are acidic, 7 is neutral, and above 7 is basic/alkaline.

question_text: Which type of mirror is used in a car's headlight to give a parallel beam of light?
raw_text: Which type of mirror is used in a car's headlight to give a parallel beam of light?
explanation: Concave mirrors converge light. When a bulb is placed at the focal point, reflected rays travel parallel — ideal for headlights and torches.

question_text: What is the main difference between arteries and veins?
raw_text: What is the main difference between arteries and veins?
options: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood to the heart
Veins carry blood away from the heart; arteries carry blood to the heart
Both carry blood in the same direction
Arteries have valves; veins do not
raw_options: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood to the heart
Veins carry blood away from the heart; arteries carry blood to the heart
Both carry blood in the same direction
Arteries have valves; veins do not
correct_answer: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood to the heart
explanation: Arteries (thick-walled) carry oxygenated blood away from the heart; veins (with valves) return blood to the heart.

question_text: What causes a rainbow to form?
raw_text: What causes a rainbow to form?
options: Refraction and dispersion of sunlight through water droplets
raw_options: Refraction and dispersion of sunlight through water droplets
correct_answer: Refraction and dispersion of sunlight through water droplets
explanation: Sunlight refracts and disperses into its component colours (ROYGBIV) as it passes through raindrops, then reflects internally to form a rainbow.

question_text: An acid and a base react to form salt and water. What is this type of reaction called?
raw_text: An acid and a base react to form salt and water. What is this type of reaction called?
explanation: Neutralisation reactions occur when an acid reacts with a base, producing a salt and water, e.g., HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O.

question_text: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination?
raw_text: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination?
explanation: The cerebellum (Latin: 'little brain') is responsible for muscle coordination, posture, and balance.

question_text: A sprinter's leg muscles begin to ache during an intense 100-metre dash because they are breaking down glucose for quick energy without enough oxygen reaching them in time. What is this process called?
raw_text: A sprinter's leg muscles begin to ache during an intense 100-metre dash because they are breaking down glucose for quick energy without enough oxygen reaching them in time. What is this process called?
explanation: Anaerobic respiration breaks down glucose without oxygen, producing less energy and by-products like lactic acid, which causes the aching sensation.

question_text: Which scientist proposed the law of universal gravitation?
raw_text: Which scientist proposed the law of universal gravitation?
explanation: Isaac Newton formulated the law of universal gravitation, explaining that every mass attracts every other mass.

question_text: Over many centuries, a tall rock formation along a coastline has been gradually worn down and reshaped by crashing waves and strong winds. What is this gradual wearing-away process called?
raw_text: Over many centuries, a tall rock formation along a coastline has been gradually worn down and reshaped by crashing waves and strong winds. What is this gradual wearing-away process called?
explanation: Erosion is the process by which natural agents like wind, water, and ice wear away and transport rock and soil.

question_text: In the human respiratory system, where does gas exchange actually take place?
raw_text: In the human respiratory system, where does gas exchange actually take place?
explanation: Alveoli are tiny air sacs in the lungs where oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged with the blood capillaries.

question_text: Which type of chemical bond involves the transfer of electrons from one atom to another?
raw_text: Which type of chemical bond involves the transfer of electrons from one atom to another?
explanation: Ionic bonds form when one atom donates electrons to another, creating oppositely charged ions that attract each other (e.g., NaCl).

question_text: A 100W appliance runs for 10 hours daily. How much energy (in kWh) does it consume in a day?
raw_text: A 100W appliance runs for 10 hours daily. How much energy (in kWh) does it consume in a day?
explanation: Energy=Power×Time=100W×10h=1000 Wh=1 kWh.

question_text: Which process explains why the Earth has seasons?
raw_text: Which process explains why the Earth has seasons?
options: Earth's distance from the Sun varies greatly
Earth's tilted axis as it orbits the Sun
The Moon blocks sunlight at different times
The Sun's energy output changes seasonally
raw_options: Earth's distance from the Sun varies greatly
Earth's tilted axis as it orbits the Sun
The Moon blocks sunlight at different times
The Sun's energy output changes seasonally
correct_answer: Earth's tilted axis as it orbits the Sun
explanation: Earth's 23.5° axial tilt means different hemispheres receive more direct sunlight at different points in its orbit, causing seasons.

question_text: What is the function of xylem and phloem in plants?
raw_text: What is the function of xylem and phloem in plants?
options: Xylem transports food; phloem transports water
Xylem transports water; phloem transports food
raw_options: Xylem transports food; phloem transports water
Xylem transports water; phloem transports food
correct_answer: Xylem transports water; phloem transports food
explanation: Xylem carries water and minerals upward from roots; phloem transports food (sugars) made in leaves to other parts of the plant.

question_text: Which of the following best describes Newton's Second Law of Motion?
raw_text: Which of the following best describes Newton's Second Law of Motion?
options: Objects at rest stay at rest
Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
Energy cannot be created or destroyed
raw_options: Objects at rest stay at rest
Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
Energy cannot be created or destroyed
explanation: Newton's Second Law: F=ma. The force on an object equals its mass multiplied by its acceleration.

question_text: A geneticist explains that a sperm cell carries only half the usual number of chromosomes, since it will combine with an egg cell to restore the full set after fertilisation. What term describes this half-set of chromosomes?
raw_text: A geneticist explains that a sperm cell carries only half the usual number of chromosomes, since it will combine with an egg cell to restore the full set after fertilisation. What term describes this half-set of chromosomes?
explanation: The haploid number (n) is half the diploid number, representing chromosomes from one parent (found in gametes/sex cells).

question_text: A botanist monitoring a greenhouse overnight, after the lights are switched off and photosynthesis stops, observes the plants still consuming one gas and releasing another. What is happening?
raw_text: A botanist monitoring a greenhouse overnight, after the lights are switched off and photosynthesis stops, observes the plants still consuming one gas and releasing another. What is happening?
options: Carbon dioxide is released; oxygen is absorbed for respiration
Oxygen is released; carbon dioxide is absorbed
No gas exchange occurs at night
raw_options: Carbon dioxide is released; oxygen is absorbed for respiration
Oxygen is released; carbon dioxide is absorbed
No gas exchange occurs at night
correct_answer: Carbon dioxide is released; oxygen is absorbed for respiration
explanation: At night, without sunlight, plants cannot photosynthesise but continue respiration — absorbing O₂ and releasing CO₂.

question_text: What is the Doppler effect commonly used for in real life?
raw_text: What is the Doppler effect commonly used for in real life?
options: Detecting speed of vehicles (radar) and weather patterns
raw_options: Detecting speed of vehicles (radar) and weather patterns
correct_answer: Detecting speed of vehicles (radar) and weather patterns
explanation: Police radar guns and Doppler weather radar use the Doppler effect — shift in frequency due to motion — to measure speed and storm movement.

question_text: Which layer of the Earth is liquid and generates Earth's magnetic field?
raw_text: Which layer of the Earth is liquid and generates Earth's magnetic field?
explanation: The molten liquid outer core, mainly iron and nickel, generates Earth's magnetic field through convective currents (geodynamo).

question_text: A patient's skin cells, after years of sun exposure, begin to show an unusual and unexpected change deep within their genetic code, increasing their cancer risk. What term describes this kind of change?
raw_text: A patient's skin cells, after years of sun exposure, begin to show an unusual and unexpected change deep within their genetic code, increasing their cancer risk. What term describes this kind of change?
explanation: A mutation is a change in the DNA sequence. It can be inherited and may lead to new traits, contributing to evolution over time.

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes static and kinetic friction?
raw_text: Which of the following correctly describes static and kinetic friction?
options: Static friction acts on moving objects; kinetic on stationary
Static friction prevents starting motion; kinetic acts during motion
Both are identical in all situations
Kinetic friction is always greater than static friction
raw_options: Static friction acts on moving objects; kinetic on stationary
Static friction prevents starting motion; kinetic acts during motion
Both are identical in all situations
Kinetic friction is always greater than static friction
correct_answer: Static friction prevents starting motion; kinetic acts during motion
explanation: Static friction must be overcome to start movement; kinetic friction acts once an object is already moving, and is usually slightly less than maximum static friction.

question_text: What are isobars used to show on a weather map?
raw_text: What are isobars used to show on a weather map?
explanation: Isobars are lines connecting points of equal atmospheric pressure, helping predict wind patterns and weather systems.

question_text: Sailors on long ocean voyages centuries ago often developed bleeding gums and extreme weakness due to a lack of fresh fruits in their diet, a condition eventually traced to a single vitamin deficiency. Which vitamin deficiency causes this disease, known as scurvy?
raw_text: Sailors on long ocean voyages centuries ago often developed bleeding gums and extreme weakness due to a lack of fresh fruits in their diet, a condition eventually traced to a single vitamin deficiency. Which vitamin deficiency causes this disease, known as scurvy?
explanation: Scurvy results from prolonged Vitamin C deficiency, causing weakness, gum disease, and poor wound healing — a problem historically common among sailors lacking fresh produce.

question_text: What is the function of the small intestine in digestion?
raw_text: What is the function of the small intestine in digestion?
options: Absorbs most nutrients into the bloodstream
raw_options: Absorbs most nutrients into the bloodstream
correct_answer: Absorbs most nutrients into the bloodstream
explanation: The small intestine, lined with villi, is the primary site of nutrient absorption into the bloodstream after enzymatic digestion.

question_text: What does a seismograph measure?
raw_text: What does a seismograph measure?
explanation: A seismograph detects and records ground vibrations caused by earthquakes, helping determine magnitude and epicentre.

question_text: Environmental scientists studying damaged forests downwind of a coal power plant trace the harm to a particular gas that reacts with water vapour in the atmosphere to form a harmful acid. Which gas is the primary cause of this acid rain?
raw_text: Environmental scientists studying damaged forests downwind of a coal power plant trace the harm to a particular gas that reacts with water vapour in the atmosphere to form a harmful acid. Which gas is the primary cause of this acid rain?
explanation: Sulphur dioxide (from burning fossil fuels) reacts with water vapour in the atmosphere to form sulphuric acid, causing acid rain.

question_text: What happens during the photoelectric effect?
raw_text: What happens during the photoelectric effect?
options: Electrons are absorbed by a metal
Light is converted directly into heat
Electrons are emitted from a metal surface when light hits it
raw_options: Electrons are absorbed by a metal
Light is converted directly into heat
Electrons are emitted from a metal surface when light hits it
correct_answer: Electrons are emitted from a metal surface when light hits it
explanation: The photoelectric effect (explained by Einstein) shows light energy can eject electrons from a metal's surface — proof of light's particle nature.

question_text: What is the universal blood donor type, and why?
raw_text: What is the universal blood donor type, and why?
options: AB positive, because it has all antigens
O negative, because it lacks A, B, and Rh antigens
B positive, because it is most common
A negative, because it is rare
raw_options: AB positive, because it has all antigens
O negative, because it lacks A, B, and Rh antigens
B positive, because it is most common
A negative, because it is rare
correct_answer: O negative, because it lacks A, B, and Rh antigens

question_text: Geographers comparing peaks around the globe agree that one towers above every other peak on the planet. Complete this sentence: 'This is the ___ mountain in the world.'
raw_text: Geographers comparing peaks around the globe agree that one towers above every other peak on the planet. Complete this sentence: 'This is the ___ mountain in the world.'
explanation: For one-syllable adjectives, the superlative is formed with '-est': high → highest, since this mountain is being compared to ALL others.

question_text: Looking at tomorrow's revision timetable, Meena sees she is scheduled to be in the middle of studying at exactly 6 PM. Which sentence correctly describes this using future continuous tense?
raw_text: Looking at tomorrow's revision timetable, Meena sees she is scheduled to be in the middle of studying at exactly 6 PM. Which sentence correctly describes this using future continuous tense?
options: She will be studying at 6 PM tomorrow.
raw_options: She will be studying at 6 PM tomorrow.
correct_answer: She will be studying at 6 PM tomorrow.
explanation: Future continuous (will be + present participle) describes an action that will be ongoing at a specific future time — here, 6 PM tomorrow.

question_text: A newspaper describes a newly built stadium as being far bigger than any other building in the city. Which word is closest in meaning to 'enormous' in this context?
raw_text: A newspaper describes a newly built stadium as being far bigger than any other building in the city. Which word is closest in meaning to 'enormous' in this context?
explanation: 'Huge' means very large, matching the meaning of 'enormous' used to describe the stadium's size.

question_text: In the sentence 'The cat hid beneath the table,' which word tells us the cat's position relative to the table?
raw_text: In the sentence 'The cat hid beneath the table,' which word tells us the cat's position relative to the table?
explanation: 'Beneath' shows the relationship of position (below/under) between the cat and the table — making it a preposition.

question_text: A shipping company moves goods from a factory in one city to stores in another city using trucks and ships. Which word best describes what this company does?
raw_text: A shipping company moves goods from a factory in one city to stores in another city using trucks and ships. Which word best describes what this company does?
explanation: 'Transport' means to carry something from one place to another — exactly what the shipping company does.

question_text: Two runners, Tom and Jerry, are competing in a race, but only one of them can come in first place. Complete this sentence: 'Either Tom ___ Jerry will win the race.'
raw_text: Two runners, Tom and Jerry, are competing in a race, but only one of them can come in first place. Complete this sentence: 'Either Tom ___ Jerry will win the race.'
explanation: 'Either...or' is the correct paired conjunction used to present a choice between two possibilities.

question_text: A nurse is praised for always paying close attention to her patients' needs and never being negligent. Which word, formed by adding a suffix to 'care', best describes her?
raw_text: A nurse is praised for always paying close attention to her patients' needs and never being negligent. Which word, formed by adding a suffix to 'care', best describes her?
explanation: The suffix '-ful' converts the noun 'care' into the adjective 'careful', meaning attentive and showing care.

question_text: A cat is grooming itself, carefully cleaning one of its own paws with its tongue. Which sentence correctly uses 'its' to describe this?
raw_text: A cat is grooming itself, carefully cleaning one of its own paws with its tongue. Which sentence correctly uses 'its' to describe this?
explanation: 'Its' (no apostrophe) shows possession. 'It's' (with apostrophe) means 'it is'. Since the paw belongs to the cat, we write 'its paw'.

question_text: A wealthy donor gives away most of his fortune to help orphanages, never asking for anything in return. Which word is the OPPOSITE of how he behaves?
raw_text: A wealthy donor gives away most of his fortune to help orphanages, never asking for anything in return. Which word is the OPPOSITE of how he behaves?
explanation: 'Generous' (willing to give freely) is the opposite of 'selfish' (concerned mainly with one's own interests) — exactly the opposite of the donor's behaviour.

question_text: Looking at the clock, Tina realises her sister has been continuously busy with chores since morning, without a single break. In 'She has been working all day,' which phrase shows this continuous action?
raw_text: Looking at the clock, Tina realises her sister has been continuously busy with chores since morning, without a single break. In 'She has been working all day,' which phrase shows this continuous action?
explanation: 'Has been working' is the complete verb phrase, showing the present perfect continuous tense for an ongoing action.

question_text: A curious child looks up during sunset and turns to her parent with a question about the sky's colour. What type of sentence is 'Why is the sky blue?'
raw_text: A curious child looks up during sunset and turns to her parent with a question about the sky's colour. What type of sentence is 'Why is the sky blue?'
explanation: An interrogative sentence asks a question and ends with a question mark — exactly what the child is doing.

question_text: A librarian hands out exactly one book to every student in line, one at a time. Complete this sentence: 'Each of the students ___ a book.'
raw_text: A librarian hands out exactly one book to every student in line, one at a time. Complete this sentence: 'Each of the students ___ a book.'
explanation: 'Each' is always singular, even when followed by 'of the students' (a plural phrase). The verb must agree: 'has'.

question_text: A student studying earthquakes, rocks, and mountains is taking a class whose Greek-rooted name reflects its subject. What does the prefix 'geo-' in this subject's name mean?
raw_text: A student studying earthquakes, rocks, and mountains is taking a class whose Greek-rooted name reflects its subject. What does the prefix 'geo-' in this subject's name mean?
explanation: 'Geo-' comes from the Greek word 'ge', meaning Earth — found in words like geography, geology, and geometry.

question_text: Listing her favourite fruits for a class project, Mira wants to separate each item clearly without using unnecessary punctuation. Which sentence does this correctly?
raw_text: Listing her favourite fruits for a class project, Mira wants to separate each item clearly without using unnecessary punctuation. Which sentence does this correctly?
options: My favourite fruits are apples, bananas and grapes.
My favourite fruits are: apples, bananas, and grapes.

My favourite fruits, are apples, bananas, and grapes.

My favourite fruits are apples bananas and grapes.
My favourite fruits, are apples, bananas, and grapes.
correct_answer: My favourite fruits are apples, bananas and grapes.
explanation: Commas separate items in a list. No colon is needed here, since there's no formal introduction before the list begins.

question_text: A coach shouts instructions to his team during practice: 'Run! Jump! Swim faster!' One word in his list of commands does not actually describe an action. Which word from this group is it?
raw_text: A coach shouts instructions to his team during practice: 'Run! Jump! Swim faster!' One word in his list of commands does not actually describe an action. Which word from this group is it?
explanation: Run, jump, and swim are action verbs describing movement. 'Quick' is an adjective describing speed, not an action itself.

question_text: Looking at her course schedule, Asha realises she is on track to finish all her required credits before next year begins. Complete: 'By next year, she ___ her degree.'
raw_text: Looking at her course schedule, Asha realises she is on track to finish all her required credits before next year begins. Complete: 'By next year, she ___ her degree.'
explanation: Future perfect (will have + past participle) describes an action that will be finished before a specific point in the future.

question_text: Despite being offered extra pocket money, Sam still hesitates and seems unwilling to help with the chores. Which word best describes Sam's attitude?
raw_text: Despite being offered extra pocket money, Sam still hesitates and seems unwilling to help with the chores. Which word best describes Sam's attitude?
explanation: 'Reluctant' means hesitant or unwilling to do something — exactly matching Sam's hesitation despite the incentive.

question_text: Comparing two singers' performances at a talent show, the judges agree that one clearly outperforms the other vocally. Complete: 'She sings better ___ I do.'
raw_text: Comparing two singers' performances at a talent show, the judges agree that one clearly outperforms the other vocally. Complete: 'She sings better ___ I do.'
explanation: 'Than' is used in comparative statements. 'Better than I do' is the correct way to compare the two performances.

question_text: After weighing all the options carefully, the committee finally reaches a final choice about which candidate to hire. What is the noun that names this outcome, formed from the verb 'decide'?
raw_text: After weighing all the options carefully, the committee finally reaches a final choice about which candidate to hire. What is the noun that names this outcome, formed from the verb 'decide'?

question_text: A florist arranging a bouquet picks out a rose, a tulip, and a daisy, then accidentally grabs something from the wrong shelf. Which item does not belong in her flower bouquet?
raw_text: A florist arranging a bouquet picks out a rose, a tulip, and a daisy, then accidentally grabs something from the wrong shelf. Which item does not belong in her flower bouquet?
explanation: Rose, tulip, and daisy are all flowers, while maple is a type of tree — making it the odd one out in a flower bouquet.

question_text: Among all the countries she had visited across Europe, Sara always says one stood out as her very first stop on that continent. Complete: '___ European country I visited was France.'
raw_text: Among all the countries she had visited across Europe, Sara always says one stood out as her very first stop on that continent. Complete: '___ European country I visited was France.'
explanation: Since this refers to one specific country out of all the ones she visited, the definite article 'the' is used here.

question_text: A botanist labelling several spiky desert plants in a display case needs to write the plural form correctly on her chart. What is the correct plural of 'cactus'?
raw_text: A botanist labelling several spiky desert plants in a display case needs to write the plural form correctly on her chart. What is the correct plural of 'cactus'?
explanation: 'Cactus' has two acceptable plural forms: the English 'cactuses' and the Latin-derived 'cacti'.

question_text: After sitting through a presentation that dragged on far longer than expected, most of the audience grew restless and stopped paying attention. Which word could replace 'lengthy' without changing the meaning of 'The lengthy speech bored everyone'?
raw_text: After sitting through a presentation that dragged on far longer than expected, most of the audience grew restless and stopped paying attention. Which word could replace 'lengthy' without changing the meaning of 'The lengthy speech bored everyone'?
explanation: 'Lengthy' means extended in duration — a synonym for 'long', matching the drawn-out speech described.

question_text: Searching for a missing novel, Dev finally finds it resting on a shelf in the family library, exactly where his sister had left it. In 'The book on the shelf belongs to me,' which phrase tells us WHERE the book is located?
raw_text: Searching for a missing novel, Dev finally finds it resting on a shelf in the family library, exactly where his sister had left it. In 'The book on the shelf belongs to me,' which phrase tells us WHERE the book is located?
explanation: 'On the shelf' begins with the preposition 'on' followed by the noun phrase 'the shelf' — together forming a prepositional phrase showing location.

question_text: During a heated argument, Priya accidentally reveals a surprise that the whole family had been carefully keeping secret for weeks. Which idiom best describes what Priya has done?
raw_text: During a heated argument, Priya accidentally reveals a surprise that the whole family had been carefully keeping secret for weeks. Which idiom best describes what Priya has done?
explanation: This idiom means to accidentally or carelessly reveal secret information — exactly what Priya did during the argument.

question_text: A student proofreading her essay circles a word she is unsure about, since she always confuses it with a similar-sounding misspelling. Which spelling is correct?
raw_text: A student proofreading her essay circles a word she is unsure about, since she always confuses it with a similar-sounding misspelling. Which spelling is correct?
explanation: 'Definitely' is correctly spelled. A useful memory trick: the word contains 'finite' inside it (defi-NITE-ly).

question_text: An art critic describes a painting using a word that conveys how visually pleasing and lovely the artwork is. Which adjective, formed from the noun 'beauty', fits this description?
raw_text: An art critic describes a painting using a word that conveys how visually pleasing and lovely the artwork is. Which adjective, formed from the noun 'beauty', fits this description?
explanation: 'Beautiful' is the adjective form of the noun 'beauty', describing something that possesses beauty.

question_text: Comparing two friends' heights, one is measured to be a few centimetres above the other, but not by an extreme amount. Which sentence uses the comparative correctly?

She is the tallest than me.

She is the tallest than me.
explanation: One-syllable adjectives form comparatives with '-er': tall → taller. We never double it with 'more' (avoid 'more taller').

question_text: Despite a rocky start to the season, the players have improved steadily and now perform impressively as a group in every match. Complete: 'The team ___ playing well this season.'
raw_text: Despite a rocky start to the season, the players have improved steadily and now perform impressively as a group in every match. Complete: 'The team ___ playing well this season.'
explanation: 'Team' is a collective noun acting as a single unit here, so it takes a singular verb: 'is playing'.

question_text: After a season of heavy rainfall, farmers report that fruit on their trees is so plentiful this year that baskets overflow at every harvest. Which word is the OPPOSITE of 'abundant' in describing a poor harvest instead?
raw_text: After a season of heavy rainfall, farmers report that fruit on their trees is so plentiful this year that baskets overflow at every harvest. Which word is the OPPOSITE of 'abundant' in describing a poor harvest instead?
explanation: 'Abundant' means existing in large quantities. Its antonym, 'scarce', means insufficient or limited in supply — the opposite of this year's plentiful harvest.

question_text: In a famous speech, Abraham Lincoln described democracy as 'government of the people, by the people, for the people,' repeating the same phrase structure three times in a row. Which rhetorical device is this?
raw_text: In a famous speech, Abraham Lincoln described democracy as 'government of the people, by the people, for the people,' repeating the same phrase structure three times in a row. Which rhetorical device is this?
explanation: Anaphora is the repetition of a word or phrase at the beginning of successive clauses: 'of the people, by the people, for the people' repeats this structure.

question_text: Which term describes words like 'because', 'since', 'although', used to join clauses of unequal rank?
raw_text: Which term describes words like 'because', 'since', 'although', used to join clauses of unequal rank?
explanation: Subordinating conjunctions introduce dependent (subordinate) clauses and link them to independent (main) clauses.

question_text: What is the grammatical function of the underlined phrase: 'To win the championship was her dream.'
raw_text: What is the grammatical function of the underlined phrase: 'To win the championship was her dream.'

question_text: Choose the sentence with correct punctuation using a colon.

question_text: What literary term describes giving hints of what is to come later in a story?
raw_text: What literary term describes giving hints of what is to come later in a story?
explanation: Foreshadowing is a literary device where the author hints at future events in the plot, building anticipation or tension.

question_text: Looking back regretfully at a missed warning, a character sighs: 'If only she had listened to me.' What mood does this sentence express?
raw_text: Looking back regretfully at a missed warning, a character sighs: 'If only she had listened to me.' What mood does this sentence express?
explanation: This expresses a hypothetical wish or regret about the past — a classic subjunctive mood construction.

question_text: Which figure of speech is in: 'All the world's a stage, and all the men and women merely players'?
raw_text: Which figure of speech is in: 'All the world's a stage, and all the men and women merely players'?
explanation: Shakespeare compares the world to a stage and people to actors throughout an extended passage — this sustained comparison is an extended metaphor.

explanation: Third conditional (past hypothetical): If + past perfect, would have + past participle. Used for situations that didn't happen in the past.

question_text: In a horror film, a character confidently announces, 'Nothing bad can happen now,' just moments before the audience — who already knows a monster is hiding nearby — watches disaster strike. What type of irony is this?
raw_text: In a horror film, a character confidently announces, 'Nothing bad can happen now,' just moments before the audience — who already knows a monster is hiding nearby — watches disaster strike. What type of irony is this?
explanation: Dramatic irony occurs when the audience knows something the character doesn't — here, the audience anticipates the danger the character is unaware of.

question_text: A surgeon double-checks every instrument and re-reads every chart twice before beginning an operation, leaving absolutely nothing to chance. Which word best describes this level of care?
raw_text: A surgeon double-checks every instrument and re-reads every chart twice before beginning an operation, leaving absolutely nothing to chance. Which word best describes this level of care?

question_text: In a narrative, what is the term for the perspective from which a story is told?
raw_text: In a narrative, what is the term for the perspective from which a story is told?

question_text: Which word best fills the blank? 'Despite the ___ evidence against him, the jury found him not guilty.'

question_text: What is the grammatical name for words like 'both...and', 'either...or', 'neither...nor'?
raw_text: What is the grammatical name for words like 'both...and', 'either...or', 'neither...nor'?
explanation: Correlative conjunctions work in pairs to join related sentence elements of equal grammatical rank.

question_text: What literary technique is it when an author directly addresses the reader?
raw_text: What literary technique is it when an author directly addresses the reader?
explanation: Direct address occurs when a narrator or character speaks straight to the reader/audience, breaking the narrative frame.

question_text: On the phone, Raj told his friend, 'I will call you tomorrow.' Reporting this conversation a week later, which sentence correctly uses reported speech?
raw_text: On the phone, Raj told his friend, 'I will call you tomorrow.' Reporting this conversation a week later, which sentence correctly uses reported speech?

correct_answer: He said that he would call me the next day.
explanation: In reported speech: 'will' shifts to 'would', and 'tomorrow' shifts to 'the next day' since the time reference has changed by the time it's reported.

question_text: A philosopher poses the riddle: 'The only constant in life is change.' At first this seems contradictory, since 'constant' and 'change' appear opposite, yet it reveals a deeper truth. What literary term describes such a statement?
raw_text: A philosopher poses the riddle: 'The only constant in life is change.' At first this seems contradictory, since 'constant' and 'change' appear opposite, yet it reveals a deeper truth. What literary term describes such a statement?

question_text: Which option correctly identifies the clause type: 'The book that you gave me was wonderful.'
raw_text: Which option correctly identifies the clause type: 'The book that you gave me was wonderful.'

question_text: A professor's lecture stretches on for two extra hours, repeating the same point in five different ways when one sentence would have sufficed. Which word best describes this kind of speech?
raw_text: A professor's lecture stretches on for two extra hours, repeating the same point in five different ways when one sentence would have sufficed. Which word best describes this kind of speech?
explanation: 'Verbose' describes speech or writing that uses far more words than needed to express an idea, like the professor's overly long lecture.

question_text: On a gloomy, overcast afternoon, one warm glance from a stranger suddenly lifts everyone's mood, as if the sun itself had broken through the clouds. Which literary device describes 'Her smile was a ray of sunshine on a cloudy day'?
raw_text: On a gloomy, overcast afternoon, one warm glance from a stranger suddenly lifts everyone's mood, as if the sun itself had broken through the clouds. Which literary device describes 'Her smile was a ray of sunshine on a cloudy day'?

question_text: What is the term for the central message or insight conveyed by a literary work?
raw_text: What is the term for the central message or insight conveyed by a literary work?

question_text: During a difficult conversation, a manager tells her employee exactly what she thinks about his work, without softening the truth or avoiding the issue. Which word best describes her honest, direct approach?

raw_text: A volunteer spends every weekend at a shelter helping strangers, never asking for money or recognition in return for her time. Which word best describes her selfless motivation?

question_text: Despite the pouring rain outside, two friends decided to go for a walk anyway, and by the time they got home, both were completely drenched. Identify the type of sentence: 'Although it was raining, we went for a walk, and we got soaked.'
raw_text: Despite the pouring rain outside, two friends decided to go for a walk anyway, and by the time they got home, both were completely drenched. Identify the type of sentence: 'Although it was raining, we went for a walk, and we got soaked.'
explanation: This sentence has one dependent clause ('Although it was raining') and two independent clauses joined by 'and' — making it compound-complex.

question_text: A diver is 8 metres above sea level on a diving platform, then dives down 15 metres into the water. Using negative numbers for depth below sea level, what is his final position relative to sea level?
raw_text: A diver is 8 metres above sea level on a diving platform, then dives down 15 metres into the water. Using negative numbers for depth below sea level, what is his final position relative to sea level?
explanation: Starting position +8, then descending 15: 8 + (−15) = −7, meaning he is 7 metres below sea level.

question_text: A scientist records temperature changes over 9 days, each day dropping by 6°C from where it started at 0°C, but then reverses direction for 6 more days, rising at the same rate. If you multiply the daily rate (−6) by the number of reversal days expressed as (−9), what do you get?
raw_text: A scientist records temperature changes over 9 days, each day dropping by 6°C from where it started at 0°C, but then reverses direction for 6 more days, rising at the same rate. If you multiply the daily rate (−6) by the number of reversal days expressed as (−9), what do you get?
explanation: Negative × Negative = Positive. (−6) × (−9) = 54, since multiplying two negative numbers gives a positive result.

question_text: A gardener buys 4x saplings, then receives 6x more as a donation, but later gives away 3x of them to a neighbour. How many saplings does he have left, in terms of x?
raw_text: A gardener buys 4x saplings, then receives 6x more as a donation, but later gives away 3x of them to a neighbour. How many saplings does he have left, in terms of x?
explanation: Combine like terms: 4x + 6x − 3x = (4+6−3)x = 7x.

question_text: Two robots on a factory line complete a task every 18 seconds and every 24 seconds respectively. If both robots finish a task right now at the same moment, after how many seconds will they next finish together?
raw_text: Two robots on a factory line complete a task every 18 seconds and every 24 seconds respectively. If both robots finish a task right now at the same moment, after how many seconds will they next finish together?
explanation: The robots align again at the LCM of 18 and 24. Multiples of 18: 18,36,54,72…; of 24: 24,48,72… LCM = 72 seconds.

explanation: Ribosomes are the cell organelles where proteins are synthesised by translating messenger RNA (mRNA) into amino acid chains.

question_text: A textbook explains that every living thing, from a single bacterium to a giant tree, is built from the same basic structural and functional unit. What is this unit called?
raw_text: A textbook explains that every living thing, from a single bacterium to a giant tree, is built from the same basic structural and functional unit. What is this unit called?
explanation: The cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of all living organisms.

question_text: A campfire turns a log into ash, smoke, and heat, and once it's done, the log can never be turned back into wood. Which type of change does this represent?
raw_text: A campfire turns a log into ash, smoke, and heat, and once it's done, the log can never be turned back into wood. Which type of change does this represent?
explanation: Burning is a chemical change — wood reacts with oxygen to form new substances (ash, CO₂, water vapour) and cannot be reversed.

question_text: A doctor explains that a dome-shaped muscle beneath the lungs contracts and relaxes with every breath a patient takes. Which structure is being described?
raw_text: A doctor explains that a dome-shaped muscle beneath the lungs contracts and relaxes with every breath a patient takes. Which structure is being described?
explanation: The diaphragm is a dome-shaped muscle below the lungs that contracts and relaxes to facilitate inhalation and exhalation.

question_text: A chemistry student dissolves salt completely into water, so that no grains remain visible and the liquid looks perfectly clear throughout. What type of mixture has she created?
raw_text: A chemistry student dissolves salt completely into water, so that no grains remain visible and the liquid looks perfectly clear throughout. What type of mixture has she created?
explanation: A solution is a homogeneous mixture where the solute (salt) is completely and uniformly dissolved in the solvent (water).

question_text: A scale at the market weighs out 2 of a certain unit of fruit, the same base SI unit used worldwide for weighing objects. What is this unit?
raw_text: A scale at the market weighs out 2 of a certain unit of fruit, the same base SI unit used worldwide for weighing objects. What is this unit?
explanation: The kilogram (kg) is the base SI unit of mass.

question_text: Astronomers comparing planets find that one massive planet completes a full spin on its axis in only about 10 hours, despite being the largest in the Solar System. Which planet is this?
raw_text: Astronomers comparing planets find that one massive planet completes a full spin on its axis in only about 10 hours, despite being the largest in the Solar System. Which planet is this?
explanation: Jupiter rotates very fast, completing one rotation in about 10 hours despite being the largest planet in the Solar System.

question_text: A doctor explains that tiny filtering units inside each kidney work non-stop to clean a patient's blood and produce urine. What are these filtering units called?
raw_text: A doctor explains that tiny filtering units inside each kidney work non-stop to clean a patient's blood and produce urine. What are these filtering units called?
explanation: Nephrons are the functional units of the kidney, filtering blood to remove waste and excess substances, forming urine.

question_text: A physics teacher asks students to describe a car's motion not just by how fast it goes, but also which direction it is heading. Which of these quantities includes both speed and direction?
raw_text: A physics teacher asks students to describe a car's motion not just by how fast it goes, but also which direction it is heading. Which of these quantities includes both speed and direction?
explanation: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, making it a vector quantity, unlike speed (which is scalar and has magnitude only).

question_text: A volcanologist examines a hardened black rock formed after molten lava erupted and cooled rapidly on the surface. What type of rock is this?
raw_text: A volcanologist examines a hardened black rock formed after molten lava erupted and cooled rapidly on the surface. What type of rock is this?
explanation: Igneous rocks form when molten rock (magma below ground, lava above) cools and crystallises into solid rock.

question_text: A firefighter explains that removing a particular gas from the air around a fire is one of the fastest ways to put it out. Which gas is essential for the fire to keep burning?
raw_text: A firefighter explains that removing a particular gas from the air around a fire is one of the fastest ways to put it out. Which gas is essential for the fire to keep burning?
explanation: Combustion requires oxygen to react with fuel, releasing heat and light energy. Removing oxygen starves the fire.

question_text: Polar bears have thick white fur that helps them blend into snowy surroundings and stay warm, a feature they are born with rather than something they learn. What type of adaptation is this?
raw_text: Polar bears have thick white fur that helps them blend into snowy surroundings and stay warm, a feature they are born with rather than something they learn. What type of adaptation is this?
explanation: Structural adaptations are physical features of an organism's body, like fur colour and thickness, that help it survive in its environment.

question_text: A patient who feels constantly dizzy and off-balance is referred to a specialist who examines a fluid-filled structure deep inside the ear. Which part of the ear is being checked?
raw_text: A patient who feels constantly dizzy and off-balance is referred to a specialist who examines a fluid-filled structure deep inside the ear. Which part of the ear is being checked?

question_text: A block of dry ice left in an open container slowly shrinks and disappears into a misty gas, without ever leaving behind a puddle. What is this process called?
raw_text: A block of dry ice left in an open container slowly shrinks and disappears into a misty gas, without ever leaving behind a puddle. What is this process called?
explanation: Dry ice (solid CO₂) sublimes — changing directly from solid to gas without passing through a liquid state.

question_text: A coach advises young athletes to eat eggs and lean meat regularly, since this food group is essential for repairing and building muscle tissue after exercise. Which nutrient is being recommended?
raw_text: A coach advises young athletes to eat eggs and lean meat regularly, since this food group is essential for repairing and building muscle tissue after exercise. Which nutrient is being recommended?
explanation: Proteins are made of amino acids and are essential for building and repairing muscle tissue and other body structures.

question_text: Scientists warn that a thinning gas layer high in the atmosphere is allowing more harmful Sun rays to reach the ground, increasing the risk of skin damage. Which layer is this?
raw_text: Scientists warn that a thinning gas layer high in the atmosphere is allowing more harmful Sun rays to reach the ground, increasing the risk of skin damage. Which layer is this?
explanation: The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation, protecting life on Earth.

question_text: A worker uses a long metal bar resting on a fixed point to pry a heavy rock out of the ground with much less effort than lifting it directly. What is this fixed pivot point called?
raw_text: A worker uses a long metal bar resting on a fixed point to pry a heavy rock out of the ground with much less effort than lifting it directly. What is this fixed pivot point called?

question_text: A boulder perched at the very top of a tall cliff has the capacity to cause great damage if it ever rolls down, purely because of its height above the ground. What type of energy does it have due to this position?
raw_text: A boulder perched at the very top of a tall cliff has the capacity to cause great damage if it ever rolls down, purely because of its height above the ground. What type of energy does it have due to this position?
explanation: Potential energy is stored energy based on an object's position or configuration, such as height above the ground.

question_text: A single yeast cell develops a small bud on its surface, which eventually grows and separates to become a brand new, genetically identical yeast cell. What is this reproduction method called?
raw_text: A single yeast cell develops a small bud on its surface, which eventually grows and separates to become a brand new, genetically identical yeast cell. What is this reproduction method called?
explanation: Budding is a form of asexual reproduction where a new organism develops from an outgrowth on the parent, common in yeast and hydra.

question_text: On a cold morning, water vapour in warm exhaled breath quickly turns into tiny visible droplets in the chilly outside air. What is this change in state called?
raw_text: On a cold morning, water vapour in warm exhaled breath quickly turns into tiny visible droplets in the chilly outside air. What is this change in state called?
explanation: Condensation occurs when a gas (like water vapour) loses energy and changes into a liquid.

question_text: A surgeon performing heart surgery identifies the single largest blood vessel responsible for carrying oxygen-rich blood away from the heart to the entire body. Which vessel is this?
raw_text: A surgeon performing heart surgery identifies the single largest blood vessel responsible for carrying oxygen-rich blood away from the heart to the entire body. Which vessel is this?
explanation: The aorta is the largest artery in the body, carrying oxygen-rich blood from the heart's left ventricle to all body tissues.

question_text: A botanist notices tiny pairs of cells surrounding small pores on a leaf's surface, opening and closing them throughout the day. What are these surrounding cells called?
raw_text: A botanist notices tiny pairs of cells surrounding small pores on a leaf's surface, opening and closing them throughout the day. What are these surrounding cells called?
explanation: Guard cells surround stomata and regulate their opening and closing, controlling gas exchange and water loss.

question_text: A scientist drops samples of water, ice, steam, and wood into a tank to see which one sinks lowest, indicating it packs the most mass into the same volume. Which one sinks the most among these?
raw_text: A scientist drops samples of water, ice, steam, and wood into a tank to see which one sinks lowest, indicating it packs the most mass into the same volume. Which one sinks the most among these?

question_text: Rooftop panels installed on a house absorb sunlight all day and supply power to the lights inside at night through stored electricity. What energy conversion is taking place in these panels?
raw_text: Rooftop panels installed on a house absorb sunlight all day and supply power to the lights inside at night through stored electricity. What energy conversion is taking place in these panels?
explanation: Solar panels (photovoltaic cells) convert light energy from the Sun directly into electrical energy.

question_text: A herpetologist studying reptiles explains that one particular lizard's body temperature rises and falls depending entirely on its surroundings, unlike a nearby warm-blooded bird. What term describes the lizard?
raw_text: A herpetologist studying reptiles explains that one particular lizard's body temperature rises and falls depending entirely on its surroundings, unlike a nearby warm-blooded bird. What term describes the lizard?
explanation: Lizards are reptiles and are cold-blooded (ectothermic) — their body temperature depends on the environment, unlike warm-blooded mammals and birds.

question_text: An engineer studying ocean waves measures the exact distance from the top of one wave to the top of the very next wave. What is this measurement called?
raw_text: An engineer studying ocean waves measures the exact distance from the top of one wave to the top of the very next wave. What is this measurement called?

question_text: A doctor explains that one small gland in the brain releases hormones that, in turn, control the activity of nearly every other hormone-producing gland in the body. Which gland is this?
raw_text: A doctor explains that one small gland in the brain releases hormones that, in turn, control the activity of nearly every other hormone-producing gland in the body. Which gland is this?

question_text: Coastal residents notice that the sea level near their town rises and falls predictably twice a day, largely due to the pull of a nearby celestial body. What is the main cause of this pattern?
raw_text: Coastal residents notice that the sea level near their town rises and falls predictably twice a day, largely due to the pull of a nearby celestial body. What is the main cause of this pattern?

raw_text: A jeweller is able to stretch a small lump of gold into a very long, thin wire without it snapping. Which property of metals allows this to happen?

question_text: A haematologist explains that the soft tissue inside certain bones is constantly manufacturing new red and white blood cells for the body. What is this tissue called?

question_text: Why do astronauts experience weightlessness in orbit, even though gravity still acts on them?
